title: audit-readiness-1on1-scratchpad-liam
content:
Purpose: quick personal prep for 1:1 with Maya (security lead) and follow-ups. This is a scratchpad — messy, todo-style.

Meeting goals:
- Surface biggest blockers for SOC2 readiness (controls evidence, owner gaps).
- Confirm vendor risk inventory and who owns vendor attestations.
- Agree next 30/60/90 day plan and tactical owners.
- Capture specific artifacts we need to attach to the audit portal.

Agenda (high level):
1) Status snapshot (2 min) — what I think is green/amber/red
2) Evidence gaps by control family (10 min) — IAM, change mgmt, logging, vendor mgmt
3) Vendor risk quick triage (10 min) — top 5 external systems used by Hosted/Dedicated/Private
4) Action items & owners (8 min)
5) Blockers + follow-ups (5 min)

Prep notes / talking points to bring up:
- SOC2: I mapped our controls to evidence we currently have in CONFLUENCE-SECURITY/AUDIT-2026. Most operational policies are there but documented evidence for automated config drift checks (infrastructure) is missing. Need someone to own ephemeral infra evidence collection.
- ISO27001: overlapping, but auditor will want risk treatment docs for vendor encryption KMS options in Private offering. For on-prem option, need to show KMS/HSM integration docs + key rotation logs.
- Vendor inventory: current list (rough): Sentry, Datadog, PagerDuty, HashiCorp Vault (managed), AWS KMS, Segment, Stripe, Google Workspace. Confirm which have third-party attestations (SOC2 Type II) — we likely have PDFs for some but not all.
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: clarify which vendors are in-scope per offering. Example: Private customers may manage their own KMS; we must show docs for the integration testing we do.

Evidence checklist (quick, note owners):
- IAM (owner: Arjun)
  - User access reviews (last 12 months) — need timestamped logs or completed review notes
  - SSO SAML configs + last test results
- Change management (owner: release-eng)
  - PR review workflow screenshots and change approval records (link to PRs)
  - Emergency change process documented + 3 recent examples
- Logging & monitoring (owner: observability)
  - Retention policy doc + sample query that reconstructs incident timeline (Datadog logs)
  - Alerting runbook examples (PagerDuty)
- Vendor management (owner: product-security)
  - Vendor inventory spreadsheet export + latest attestation PDFs
  - Risk assessments for top 5 vendors (briefs in Confluence)
- Data classification & handling (owner: product)
  - Data flow diagrams for Hosted API and Private on-prem
  - Example of redaction/PII handling in logs

Open questions I want to ask Maya during 1:1:
- Which control families do auditors usually probe hardest for inference platforms? My guess: change mgmt and vendor management. Confirm.
- For Redwood Private (customer-managed infra), do auditors expect us to gather customer-side evidence or only our integration test evidence?
- Are there any specific templates the auditor prefers for KMS/HSM evidence?

Risks / gotchas to call out:
- We rely on a handful of 3rd-party managed services with expiring SOC2 PDFs (last one we have is 2023). Need contact owners to refresh evidence requests. (Action: ask vendor owners for renewal timelines.)
- Some Dedicated infra automation creates short-lived instances that may not appear in long-term config snapshots — need to confirm drift-history collection.
- Private/on-prem: customer network diagrams sometimes missing; we need a template to request from SEs.

Draft asks / action items (to convert into tickets after meeting):
- TODO: Create a short runbook for evidence collection for SOC2 portal (owner: me) — include who to ping for each vendor attestation. Target: 2/28.
- TODO: Ask Arjun to export last 12 months of SSO/SAML user review evidence and drop into Confluence page (owner: Arjun). Target: 3/5.
- TODO: Coordinate with observability team to snapshot a sample incident timeline and retention policy proof (owner: Maya/observability). Target: 3/10.
- TODO: Reach out to customer success for Private deployment network diagrams template (owner: Solutions Eng). Target: 3/7.
- TODO: Inventory check — confirm which vendors have up-to-date SOC2/ISO PDFs; create a tracker column (owner: product-security). Target: 3/3.

Follow-up email template (very rough) to send after meeting:
"Hi Maya,
Thanks for the sync — here are the action items I captured and owners. I'll spin up tickets for the ones we agreed and ping owners individually. Quick summary: evidence gaps for change mgmt & vendor attestations; need KMS integration artifacts for Private.
Regards,
Liam"

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Might be useful to run a short mock-audit with internal SRE + product-security to surface awkward evidence cases. Could schedule a 90-min session.
- Check GitHub PR history for emergency changes: search label emergency or hotfix in repo infra-configs.
- Slack threads to reference: #sec-audit-2026 (pin messages), #platform-ops (for drift discussion).

Immediate next steps before 1:1 (today):
- skim CONFLUENCE-SECURITY/AUDIT-2026 and mark obvious missing pieces (15–20m)
- prepare list of vendors missing attestation PDFs (quick export from vendor sheet) (20m)
- bring up the Private KMS question explicitly

Longer timeline (30 / 60 / 90):
- 30d: get baseline evidence for IAM, logging, vendor attestations (deliverable: audit portal checklist populated)
- 60d: close change mgmt evidence gaps, run mock-audit
- 90d: freeze a 90-day evidence pack for auditors and schedule external readiness review

End of scratchpad.
(If this looks useful, I'll convert action items into JIRA and link back.)
